key_insight: This paper shows that sufficiently wide quantum physics-informed neural networks (QPINNs) can be trained in a lazy regime where the nonlinear gradient flow is accurately captured by a linearized neural tangent kernel (NTK) model.
engineering_relevance: It provides a quantitative theory for when quantum circuit-based PDE solvers can be expected to train predictably, with bounds tied to qubit count, depth, light-cone geometry, and domain dimension.
method: Analyze gradient-flow training dynamics of QPINNs for second-order elliptic PDEs with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
Use overparameterized NTK theory to derive a nonasymptotic lazy-training approximation for parameterized quantum circuits.
Prove explicit approximation bounds for both the nonlinear model and its variational formulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical, nonasymptotic analysis rather than experiments, with guarantees expressed through explicit bounds on approximation error under sufficient circuit width.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on large-width, overparameterized circuits, so practical performance may degrade for smaller or hardware-constrained quantum models.
paper_title: Lazy training of quantum physics informed neural networks
